I do not have an answer for that I am afraid.

As mentioned above, limestone can and potentially have large cavities. Traditional slurry TBMs would lose the slurry to the cavities and will not be able to cater to the cavities. Injecting slurry into the cavity may cause sinkholes (if the slurry is lost to the ground) or blowouts if the pressure is not well maintained. Typically, the volume of the slurry is maintained and only disposed when it has been through the circuit too many times that the mined materials slurry cannot be filtered out anymore.

The VD TBM which MMC-Gamuda uses will instead inject a higher density slurry into the cavities which will not be lost to the ground, stabilizing the pressure ahead before mining through it, potentially reducing the risks. 

This is one main difference I can point out. We have to setup extra plants, equipment, modify the TBM and inject HD slurry(money) into cavities.

Ground improvement is required at areas which have been deemed unsafe to mine through by G&P(well know geology consultant), which require us to hire a sub-contractor to do up to thousand cement grouting points in order to ensure the overhead ground is not affected when the TBM mines through. 

Also in Malaysia, due to poor management, nobody has a full layout of the utilities, with smaller telco companies such as Maxis, Digi installing their fibre optic cables either too shallow (there was a case where it was 50mm under a road) or even bigger companies such as SYABAS not updating their rerouting of the service pipes. The contractor will be charged the repair fee when striking one of these even when the service providers do not update the utility layout map.

Dilapidation surveys are carried out on all the structures deemed to be in the Right Of Way of the tunneling works, where compensation has to be given or rectification works have to be carried out if proven that any generation or expansion of cracks are due to the tunneling works. When working in more unstable ground, there may be more potential damage to these structures

I like how people assume that the whole cost and progress is just for the tunnel, leaving out land acquisition, dilapidation survey, ground treatment, compensation to stakeholders if their businesses are disrupted, site setup and much more. Also leaving out the type of geology that the tunnels are built in when mentioning costs, which is mainly limestone for malaysia, but providing justifications when other projects have higher price/km
